contexts.text: This state (of desolation and vastation) is called the day of His wrath and vengeance, etc.

Wrath, anger, indignation, and fury, in these passages, = turning away, opposition, and the consequent penalty. The reason the penalty of (these) is ascribed to the Lord, and is called anger, wrath, and fury, in Him, is that the (Israelites) had to be kept in the representatives of the Church...
Their wrath, for it was hard () = a turning away from truth, which was confirmed; for wrath, being predicated of truth, = a turning away from it.

Thou sendest forth Thy wrath () = the fury of cupidities, and the endeavour to inflict violence, with the evil. For wrath, when attributed to the Lord, = the destruction and punishment of the endeavours of those who oppose themselves to the Divine, and who want to inflict violence on those whom the Divine protects. This appears as if the anger and wrath were from the Divine, and yet it is in themselves. References.
Hence a man is said to grow hot, when he is angry.
By the day of wrath, etc. is meant the advent of the Lord to Judgment.
They grew so hot that a flame appeared from their nostrils.
In the heat of his faith he may say...
With the Lord, zeal is not wrath; it only appears so...
The cup of His wrath () = the truth through which is good.
In the Word, anger and wrath are frequently mentioned together, and then... wrath is predicated of falsity, because... those in falsity grow hot. Illustrated.
Therefore, if the love... is touched... and the touch hurts, there ensues wrath.
Regarded in itself, zeal is a violent heating of the natural man.
Unless it is regenerated, it is nothing but wrath against all things of faith.
The wrath, etc. of Jehovah = the Last Judgment, and the state of damnation of those who are in evils and falsities. Illustrated. AE 413:4. AE 413:6.
To be incensed against Jehovah () = to be in falsities from evil.
The cup of the wrath of His anger () = its devastation through direful falsities of evil.
